ci_method: Visit-level linear-probability DiD (hit ~ program*post), cluster-robust (CR0) standard errors clustered on practice_id (60 clusters), normal 95% interval; SE = 0.97 pp. Corroborated by wild cluster bootstrap-t with Rademacher weights, 2000 reps, null imposed ([5.90, 9.90] pp, p<0.0005) and by practice-level Welch t-test on the 60 practice-specific pre/post changes ([5.90, 9.82] pp). Randomization inference permuting the program label across the 60 practices (2000 draws) gives p<0.0005 with a null 2.5-97.5 percentile range of [-2.84, 2.81] pp.
specifications_run: PRIMARY: 2x2 visit-level LPM DiD, outcome = any PCP visit day 0-14 after ED visit, PCP = office E/M (POS 11, Family Medicine or Internal Medicine, CPT 99211-99215) OR hospital-based family-practice clinic visit (POS 22 facility, CPT G0463, revenue code 0517); ED visit = member-day with any POS 23 line; pre = Jan-Jun 2025, post = Jul-Dec 2025; SE clustered on practice. Result +7.91 pp [6.00, 9.81]

PCP definition: office E/M only (POS 11 FM/IM 99211-99215), excluding hospital-based clinic visits. Result +2.46 pp [0.60, 4.31] - DISCARDED as the primary spec because it drops ~64k provider-based primary-care clinic visits that exist in both arms before the program
PCP definition: office E/M + all POS 22 G0463 (revenue 0517 and 0519). Result +8.06 pp [6.13, 9.99]
PCP definition: hospital-based family-practice clinic (G0463 rev 0517) only. Result +6.24 pp [5.06, 7.42]
PCP definition: Family Medicine only (drop Internal Medicine) + hospital clinic rev 0517. Result +7.22 pp [5.40, 9.03]
PCP definition: any POS 11 FM/IM contact including lab-only days (CPT 36415) + hospital clinic rev 0517. Result +7.91 pp [6.00, 9.81]

PCP definition: any office E/M including specialist visits (99204/9921x, any specialty) + hospital clinic rev 0517, as an upper-bound 'any ambulatory follow-up' definition. Result +7.40 pp [5.44, 9.36]
Two-way fixed effects: practice FE + calendar-month FE, program x post interaction, cluster practice. Result +7.90 pp [5.97, 9.83]
Two-way FE + ED acuity (99281-99285) controls. Result +7.90 pp [5.97, 9.84]
Practice x period aggregate (120 cells), unweighted OLS. Result +7.86 pp [5.94, 9.82]
Practice x period aggregate, weighted by ED visit count. Result +7.91 pp [5.98, 9.84]
Practice-level diff-in-means (Welch t-test on 60 practice pre/post changes). Result +7.86 pp [5.90, 9.82], p=6e-11
Logit with program x post interaction (interaction log-odds +0.356, p<1e-4) - reported only as a functional-form check; the LPM is the estimand the review asks for (percentage points)
Alternative SE: iid/unclustered [5.80, 10.02], HC1 [5.80, 10.01], clustered on member [5.78, 10.03] - all similar, so clustering is not what drives inference
Wild cluster bootstrap-t (Rademacher, 2000 reps, null imposed): [5.90, 9.90] pp, p<0.0005
Randomization inference, permuting program assignment across the 60 practices (2000 draws): p<0.0005

Event study: practice FE + calendar-month FE with program x relative-month interactions, June 2025 as reference. Pre: -3.44, -3.91, -2.76, -2.87, +0.95 pp (Jan-May); post: +8.86, +7.97, +3.49, +4.36, +5.16, +5.57 pp (Jul-Dec)

Event study by channel: hospital-clinic channel pre-period coefficients -0.52, +0.32, -0.13, +0.15, +0.48 pp (joint F p=0.979) then +7.78, +6.88, +4.50, +6.65, +6.47, +5.53 pp - a sharp, sustained break exactly at July with no pre-trend
Placebo DiD inside the pre-period (Apr-Jun vs Jan-Mar, no real treatment): +2.71 pp [0.08, 5.35], p=0.044 - a mild pre-period divergence, investigated further below
DiD controlling for a differential linear time trend (program x month over the full year). Result +7.24 pp [3.39, 11.08]; the fitted differential trend is +0.11 pp/month (p=0.70)

Pre-trend-extrapolation-adjusted DiD (subtract 6 x the pre-period differential slope of 0.907 pp/month from the naive DiD). Result +2.47 pp, practice cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [-3.00, 7.48], 85% of bootstrap reps > 0 - the most pessimistic defensible spec; DISCARDED as the headline because the slope is estimated off 6 noisy months, is split between the two arms (treated +0.42 pp/month p=0.15, control -0.49 pp/month p=0.08, neither significant), and is absent from the channel that carries most of the effect

Channel-wise pre-trend-extrapolation adjustment: hospital-clinic channel +5.68 pp (pre-slope +0.09 pp/month, p=0.62), office channel -1.42 pp (pre-slope +0.65 pp/month, p=0.09); summing gives roughly +4.3 pp
Drop May-June from the pre-period (in case of pre-launch ramp-up/anticipation). Result +9.17 pp [7.16, 11.19]
Narrow window, May-Jun vs Jul-Aug only. Result +7.83 pp [4.33, 11.33]
Drop Jul-Aug (in case of a novelty spike). Result +6.67 pp [4.58, 8.76]
Follow-up window length: 7 days +2.20 pp [0.28, 4.12]; 14 days (primary) +7.91 pp; 30 days (ED visits restricted to on/before Dec 15 to avoid right-censoring) +6.84 pp [4.61, 9.07]
Leave-one-month-out re-estimation of the pre-period differential slope: 0.72 to 1.18 pp/month across the six drops
assumptions_checked: ED visit definition: every POS 23 member-day (31,260 in 2025) carries both a facility and a professional claim, an ED E/M code (99281-99285) and a 045x ED revenue code - all three definitions give the identical visit set, so the denominator is not definition-sensitive. Counting distinct ED facility claims instead of member-days gives 31,271 (11 same-day repeat visits), a 0.04% difference.

PCP visit definition - the one decision that actually moves the answer. Beyond POS 11 office E/M by Family/Internal Medicine, the extract contains 76,877 provider-based (hospital outpatient) clinic visits: POS 22 facility, CPT G0463, revenue 0517 ('clinic - family practice', 64,293 lines) or 0519 ('clinic - other', 12,584 lines). These are genuine primary-care encounters: they appear in all 60 practices, in both arms, and at similar rates before the program (6.3% of treated and 7.6% of control ED visits had one in the pre-period), so they are pre-existing capacity rather than program-created billing. Counting only POS 11 office visits gives +2.46 pp; including rev-0517 clinic visits gives +7.91 pp. I include them. Revenue 0519 is ambiguous (could be specialty clinic) and shows no program response (+0.15 pp when added), so excluding it is immaterial.

Specialist contamination: POS 11 E/M codes 99213/99214 are also billed by Cardiology, GI, Dermatology, Endocrinology and Orthopedics, and practice_id is the member's attributed PCP rather than the rendering practice, so specialty is the only discriminator. Restricting to FM/IM is required; a sensitivity that counts any office E/M including specialists gives +7.40 pp.

Non-visit lines excluded: CPT 36415 venipuncture (89,580 lines at POS 11 under FM/IM) and POS 81 Clinical Laboratory and POS 11 Radiology lines are not visits. Treating any FM/IM POS 11 contact as a visit changes nothing (+7.91 pp), because lab-draw days coincide with E/M days.

Right-censoring of the follow-up window: the last ED visit is 2025-12-31 and the extract runs to 2026-01-14, exactly 14 days, with 9,390 PCP office E/M lines and 2,799 G0463 lines dated in Jan 2026. December's follow-up rate (35.4% control, 37.0% program) is in line with November's, so no month is truncated. The 30-day sensitivity does need censoring protection, so it restricts ED visits to on/before Dec 15.

Treatment timing and compliance: all 30 program practices have launch_date 2025-07-01 (no staggered adoption, so no Goodman-Bacon/negative-weight problem) and all 30 control practices have a blank launch_date. All 30 treated practices increased their follow-up rate by more than the control-arm mean change (range +1.8 to +14.2 pp, mean +8.7) versus control (range -8.6 to +8.4, mean +0.9); the distributions barely overlap, so the effect is not driven by a handful of practices.

Parallel trends - the main threat, and partly violated. The joint F-test of the five pre-period event-study interactions is not significant (p=0.196), but a within-pre-period placebo DiD (Apr-Jun vs Jan-Mar) gives +2.71 pp (p=0.044) and a differential linear pre-trend gives +0.91 pp/month (p=0.023), robust to dropping any single pre month (0.72-1.18). Decomposing by channel locates the problem: the office-visit channel has a noisy upward pre-drift, while the hospital-clinic channel, which carries 6.2 of the 7.9 pp, has a flat pre-period (joint F p=0.979, coefficients between -0.52 and +0.48 pp) and a sharp sustained doubling from ~6% to ~12% starting exactly in July while the control arm stays at 7-8%. Explaining the whole naive DiD away would require a sustained differential trend of 1.32 pp/month, well above the 0.91 pp/month estimated (itself split roughly evenly between a treated rise of +0.42 pp/month, p=0.15, and a control decline of -0.49 pp/month, p=0.08, neither significant). Trend-adjusted specs span +2.5 to +9.2 pp; all are positive, so the sign is robust and the magnitude is not pinned down as tightly as the primary CI alone implies.

Composition of the denominator: ED volume is stable across arm and period (program 7,703 pre / 7,783 post; control 7,827 / 7,947), as is the ED acuity mix (99281-99285 shares within 1 pp of each other in all four cells), the number of distinct ED members, and ED visits per member (1.063-1.070). Adding acuity controls leaves the estimate at +7.90 pp, so the result is not a case-mix shift.
Attribution stability: no member appears under more than one practice_id across the whole extract, so there is no practice-switching or contamination of the treated/control contrast.

Data quality: 1,067,719 lines, no duplicate claim_id/line_no pairs, no fully duplicated rows, no negative or zero allowed amounts (so no reversals or denied-claim adjustments to net out), and ED visits present in every month of 2025 (2,423-2,692 per month, no gaps or spikes). Every pos/claim_type/revenue_code/specialty/CPT combination in the file was enumerated and classified, so no alternative primary-care coding path was missed.

Inference with few clusters: 60 practices is enough for cluster-robust SEs, and the wild cluster bootstrap and randomization inference agree closely with the asymptotic interval, so the CI is not a small-cluster artifact.

NOT checkable with this extract: member enrollment/eligibility spans are not provided, so follow-up visits can only be missed through disenrollment, not verified as observable; and rendering provider identity is absent, so I cannot confirm that a G0463 clinic visit was delivered by the member's own attributed practice.
headline_claim: The care-navigation program raised the 14-day ED-to-PCP follow-up rate by about 8 percentage points (95% CI 6.0 to 9.8), from 29% to 38% in program practices while comparison practices were flat at roughly 36%, and the gain is robust across specifications though a mild pre-existing trend means the most conservative estimate is nearer 3-4 points.
